title: Principal matrix logarithm as Richter integral of a resolvent-like kernel
expression_sketch:
Let A lie in C^{n x n} with no eigenvalues on the closed negative real axis R-. The principal logarithm log(A) is the unique logarithm of A whose eigenvalues lie in the open strip {z : -pi < Im(z) < pi}, and
  log(A) = Integral( (A - I) [t (A - I) + I]^{-1}, (t, 0, 1) ).
Scalar check written in the proof: for x in C off R-,
  log(x) = Integral( (x-1)/(t(x-1)+1), (t, 0, 1) ).
The integrand is undefined at those t in [0,1] for which -1/t is an eigenvalue of A-I, i.e. for which some eigenvalue of A equals 1 - 1/t in (-infinity, 0]; that collision is excluded by the hypothesis that spec(A) misses R-.
latent_structure: One MATRIX_FUNCTION master: the principal logarithm is the definite integral of the rational kernel (A-I)[t(A-I)+I]^{-1} along the compact parameter interval [0,1]. The same kernel on scalars is the Newton quotient of log between the nodes 1 and x, integrated in the convex combination t x + (1-t) 1. Negative-real spectrum of A is the degeneracy where the path hits a pole.

t.note: dummy of the Richter integral on [0,1]

function_domains.log: Principal matrix logarithm: unique logarithm X of A with spec(X) subset {z : -pi < Im(z) < pi}, defined if and only if A has no eigenvalues on R- (Higham Theorem 1.31, restated as the standing hypothesis of Chapter 11 and of Theorem 11.1).
function_domains.scalar_log: Principal branch of the logarithm on C minus R-.

nonzero_conditions.statement: A has no eigenvalues on R-, so in particular 0 is not an eigenvalue and A is nonsingular (Higham Chapter 11 standing hypothesis; a singular matrix has no logarithms, Theorem 1.27).
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 1.27, Theorem 1.31, Theorem 11.1

analytic_domains.statement: A in C^{n x n} has no eigenvalues on R- (Higham Theorem 11.1 hypothesis). Then log(A) exists and equals the displayed integral.
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 11.1 (Richter)

analytic_domains.statement: If A is real and has no eigenvalues on R-, then log(A) is real (Higham Theorem 1.31, recalled in the Chapter 11 preamble).
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 1.31 and Chapter 11 preamble

branch_conventions: log always denotes the principal logarithm whose spectrum lies in the strip {z : -pi < Im(z) < pi} (Higham Theorem 1.31 and Chapter 11 opening paragraph).
The scalar logarithm in the proof of Theorem 11.1 is the principal branch on C minus R-.
exp(log(A)) = A holds by definition of a logarithm; log(exp(A)) = A is a different identity and is not claimed (Higham Chapter 11, paragraph after Theorem 11.1, citing Problem 1.39).

limit_domains.statement: The Richter parameter t ranges over the compact interval [0, 1] (Higham Theorem 11.1). No improper endpoint.
limit_domains.label: DECLARED
limit_domains.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 11.1

source_provenance: N. J. Higham, Functions of Matrices: Theory and Computation, SIAM, 2008, Theorem 1.31 and Theorem 11.1 (Richter). DOI 10.1137/1.9780898717778.ch11
H. Richter, Zum Logarithmus einer Matrix, Arch. Math. 2 (1950) 360-363

derived_conditions.statement: It suffices to prove the scalar identity log(x) = Integral((x-1)/(t(x-1)+1), (t,0,1)) for x in C off R-, because the matrix identity then follows for diagonalizable A and extends by Higham Theorem 1.20 (Higham, proof of Theorem 11.1).
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 11.1 proof and Theorem 1.20

derived_conditions.statement: For x off R- the affine path t |-> 1 + t(x-1), t in [0,1], does not hit 0, so the scalar integrand has no pole on the parameter interval.
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 11.1 proof ('this latter equality is immediate' for x off R-)

public_source: N. J. Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 11.1 (Richter) and Theorem 1.31, DOI 10.1137/1.9780898717778.ch11. Original: H. Richter, Arch. Math. 2 (1950) 360-363.
why_not_cse_lgg: The expanded integrand (A-I)[t(A-I)+I]^{-1} is a rational matrix function of t; CSE will not recognise its t-integral as the principal logarithm, nor unify that integral with the spectral-strip characterisation of log(A). LGG will not invent the kernel or the R- cut.
proposer_leak_risk: Hide principal logarithm, Richter, branch strip, inverse scaling and squaring. Catalog members are the definite integral in t and the scalar integrand (x-1)/(t(x-1)+1).
notes: Do not insert holomorphy of a general f, a closed contour integral of a general f, or the identity log(exp(A))=A. Do not insert self-adjointness. The cut R- is the hypothesis of Theorem 11.1, not folklore positivity. If an eigenvalue of A lies on R- the integral is not the object claimed here; that is a different existence theorem (Culver), not a repair of Theorem 11.1.
